title: Segment Tree
tagline: A binary tree over array ranges — flexible range queries and point updates in O(log n).

complexity.time: O(log n) per op, O(n) build

intuition.analogy: An org chart where each manager reports a summary (sum, min, max) of their whole team. Ask any manager and you instantly get their subtree's stat; change one employee and only their chain of managers needs updating.
paragraphs: A segment tree stores aggregate information about array ranges in a binary tree. The root covers [0, n−1]; each node splits its range in half between two children, down to single elements at the leaves.

A range query decomposes the queried interval into O(log n) canonical node ranges and combines their stored aggregates. A point update changes one leaf and re-merges along the path to the root — also O(log n).
Unlike a Fenwick tree, it handles any associative operation (sum, min, max, gcd, …) and supports range updates with lazy propagation. It's the Swiss-army knife of range data structures.
intuition.keyIdea: Each node aggregates a range; queries combine O(log n) covering nodes, updates fix the path to the root.

steps.title: Build recursively
steps.detail: Each node merges its two children's aggregates; leaves hold single elements. Build is O(n).

steps.title: Query a range
steps.detail: If a node's range is fully inside the query, return its value; if disjoint, return the identity; else recurse into both children and merge.

steps.title: Point update
steps.detail: Descend to the target leaf, change it, and re-merge on the way back up.

complexity.time: O(log n) per query/update, O(n) build
complexity.timeReason: A range splits into O(log n) covering nodes; updates touch one root-to-leaf path.
complexity.spaceReason: About 2n–4n nodes for an array of size n.

pitfalls: Allocate ~4n nodes to be safe with the recursive indexing.
Use the correct identity for the operation (0 for sum, +∞ for min, −∞ for max).
Off-by-one in the disjoint/full-cover conditions is the most common bug.
